beats.say: A razor sells itself. And you never buy the razor again.
Buy the handle alone, no blades included.
Buy a razor plus a tiny pack of blades.
Buy the razor with a full-year blade supply.
First year: 51 razors, 168 blades. Looks generous.
But it does a job: it forces endless blade purchases.
In 1904 the razor count jumped to 90,884 while blades hit 123,648.
Each razor became a subscription to blades, so the real profit lived in the blades.
Customers bought the handle once, then kept paying for blades forever.
You see it everywhere: a coffee shop sells a $5 mug alone, a $2 pod pack, and a $5 mug + pod bundle.
A café also offers a $30 espresso machine alone, a $1-per-shot capsule subscription, and a $30 machine + starter capsule pack.
The bundled machine looks pricey, but the cheap mug with pods feels like the smart choice.
When a product includes a cheap consumable, the real profit is the consumable. Follow for more.
